Hands down, the best hospitality I have been lucky enough to receive in my entire life.

Upon arriving in leh, we were disoriented, feeling the altitude, and uncomfortable. As foreigners, we knew we had to get a permit to go into other parts of ladakh. Grudgingly, we mustered up the energy to head out onto fort road and look for a travel agent. It was the evening, around 6:30pm, when most are closed. We spotted Swiss tour and travel, and decided to enter. This decision alone made our Ladakh trop unforgettable.

We were greeted by Amo, a lovely, friendly and easygoing young lady who sorted out our permits with no fuss or issues.

The next day, we went back into Swiss Tour and Travels to ask for advice on trekking we can do around Ladakh. It was on this day that a level of hospitality I had never known was possible showed itself to me. As we were talking to Ishe Mama, the woman in charge of the agency, it started raining outside. Ishe insisted on giving us endless cups of tea, asking us about our li be an and sharing stories of her own trips. She was eating momos, and insisted that we share. She told us we can meet her son, who is just 15, and we did just that the next day.

Her son took us on a day hike up a mountain in their small village outside leh. We made a fire of wood and cooked maggi halfway up. Every single member of the family is a beautiful person with a beautiful soul, so willing to help that it reshaped my idea of what human connection could look like. Thank you, Ishe Mama (mama tea)! We will never forget you.
